data.name: Jireh
data.gender_notes: Jireh is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Lord will see, and provide; a name given to God by Abraham when he was led to the ram caught in the thicket, which he offered up instead of his son Isaac. The name Jireh carries the meaning “God will provide” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Jireh usually hope their child will grow to embody god will provide and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jireh belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God will provide.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jireh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Jireh
in_english.meaning: name of God, means the Lord will provide
in_english.long_meaning: the name of God in Hebrew, meaning the Lord will provide, as seen in the Bible, Isaiah 41:28, Isaiah 49:26, 60:16, 65:11, 65:16, 65:18, 66:22, 66:23, 66:24, 66:25, in the New Testament, and in the early Christian Church, and in Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: In African American culture, the name Jireh is popularly used as a name for boys and carries the connotation of provision and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Bible, the name Jireh holds spiritual significance as a reminder of God's faithfulness and provision, as seen in the story of Abraham's sacrifice of Isaac. It serves as a testament of God's love and care for his people.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jireh is a biblical name meaning "The Lord will provide." This name is derived from the story of Abraham, who, in his faithfulness, built an altar and named it El-Jireh, God-provides, before God intervened to supply the sacrifice for Abraham's test of faith.

historical_references.reference: Genesis 22:14, God promises Abraham a son and says: 'I will surely bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will take possession of the gate of their enemies, and in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed me.'

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Jireh remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Jireh in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Jireh, which means "God will provide". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
